extracted.intended_audience: attorneys and other practitioners before the USPTO; Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) staff and disciplinary counsel
extracted.subtask_description: A Final Order issued under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 imposing reciprocal discipline (exclusion from trademark and non-patent practice) based on a state court disbarment, specifying prohibitions, publication/notice requirements, and the reinstatement process under USPTO regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for reciprocal discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal discipline may be imposed by the Director of the USPTO pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 when an attorney has been disciplined by a duly constituted authority of a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order here was requested to be identical to the discipline imposed by the District of Columbia Court of Appeals (disbarment). The Notice and Order referenced 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 as the regulatory basis for seeking reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to respond and permissible grounds to oppose (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is given an opportunity (40 days in this matter) to file a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to the state-imposed discipline, based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order provided Respondent an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing imposition of identical reciprocal discipline based on the specific regulatory reasons enumerated in § 11.24(d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to respond (no genuine issue of material fact)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent fails to file a timely response to the Notice and Order, the Office may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In light of Respondent's failure to file a response, the Final Order determined there is no genuine issue of material fact and that exclusion from practice in trademark and other non-patent matters is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion from practice in trademark and non-patent matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent is excluded from the practice of trademark and other non-patent matters before the USPTO commencing on the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order specifies exclusion from practice of trademark and other non-patent matters before the USPTO as the appropriate discipline imposed pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration and reinstatement process (37 C.F.R. § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent remains suspended from practice before the USPTO until the OED Director grants a petition requesting reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement requires filing and grant of a petition under § 11.60; until such petition is granted the exclusion remains in effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibitions related to USPTO.gov accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: While excluded, the respondent is prohibited from (1) opening or activating any USPTO.gov account(s) used for filing trademark documents; (2) applying for or attempting to apply for such accounts; (3) verifying or attempting to verify any other person's credentials in connection with such accounts; and (4) sponsoring or attempting to sponsor such accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These specific account-related prohibitions are imposed until a reinstatement petition is granted pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO authority to prevent account actions
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO may act to prevent the respondent from opening, activating, applying for, verifying credentials for, or sponsoring USPTO.gov accounts to be used for filing trademark documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order authorizes the USPTO to take action (e.g., technical or administrative measures) to prevent the respondent from engaging in the prohibited account activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: No reactivation of suspended/terminated USPTO.gov accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: No USPTO.gov account(s) used in connection with trademark matters that are suspended, terminated, or otherwise deactivated pursuant to the imposition of this exclusion are to be unsuspended or otherwise re-activated until a petition for reinstatement is granted under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accounts deactivated because of the exclusion remain deactivated until an OED-granted reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication in OED FOIA Reading Room
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room (http://foiadocuments.uspto.gov).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order requires public posting of the Final Order in the OED FOIA Reading Room for public review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Official Gazette notice with specified content
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette describing the exclusion, the respondent's identity and location, the regulatory basis (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)), and the misconduct findings (e.g., violations of D.C. Rules of Professional Conduct 1.15(a) and 8.4(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample Notice in the Order includes: identification of the respondent, statement that respondent is excluded from practice in trademark and non-patent matters, the rule violated, findings of reckless misappropriation/commingling of trust funds and failure to keep records, and references to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to disciplinary enforcement agencies and courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the states where respondent is admitted, to courts where respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides formal notification requirements to other jurisdictions and entities that monitor attorney discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's duties upon discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order requires compliance with § 11.58 duties (which typically include giving notice to clients, withdrawing from matters as appropriate, and handling client files and funds) though the Order references the regulation rather than restating each duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority citation (35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: The action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites statutory and regulatory authority for imposing reciprocal discipline and publicizing disciplinary actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Underlying misconduct findings (D.C. Rules violations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent was found to have violated D.C. Rules of Professional Conduct 1.15(a) and 8.4(d) by recklessly misappropriating and commingling trust funds and by failing to keep adequate records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These specific misconduct findings are the predicate for the reciprocal discipline imposed by the USPTO; the Official Gazette notice example summarizes these factual findings.
